I’ve made ten jars like this, crimson pots, thrown crimson clay that’ll eventually be coated in a crimson glaze and then finally, they’ll be reduction fired, oh, there’s also some bronze in the mix, small fragments, which when put through the kiln turn into these red haloed flecks of metal. All of that might sound quite over the top but it’s a deep red with underlying tones of black and hopefully they resemble some of the tests I’ve fired in the past… fingers crossed. They require a different approach when crafting them, especially during the turning stage. As the particles of grog the body contains are constantly torn out I have to go back over the surface, burnishing it and smoothing it as I go to get rid of the overly prominent scratches these splinters of ceramic create. I lost a few pieces from attempting to fix oval openings, they were thrown round, but as clay slowly dries it’s quite common for it to subtlety warp. I tried to gentle press the opening back into a round shape and I felt something give; upon further inspection I found a hairline crack in the rim. Grogged clays might be tough during the throwing and the firing but it’s brittle stuff during the trimming stage, especially when trimmed as thinly as this. #clay #handmade #satisfying #pottery #ceramics

I’m embarking on a new round of material tests. This time, I’m seeing what molybdenum, volcanic sand, carborundum, titanium siliconite, peridot, lapis lazuli and finally, some red garnet, will do. All of which have different textures and consistencies and change how the stoneware clay throws and trims. This is the subject of my YouTube video this weekend, (a link to which you can find in the Linktree in my profile’s biography), and it’s worth noting, that this is part one of a series I’ll be producing over the next couple of weeks or month—meaning the results will come, just not quite yet. I always have a rough idea about what some of these additions will do, and in truth, it’s never quite as exciting as what you might be picturing in your mind. Often, glass and minerals melt, metals bloom and flow, and more commonly than not, things turn brown or black and are underwhelming. Yet, sometimes there’s some real gems, there are oddities that create beautiful bursts of colour, like the bronze I’ve used a lot in the past. I know that testing these on small test tiles would be “better” technique. They take up less space in the kiln and are faster to produce, yet then I wouldn’t have what’s a growing collection of somewhat unusual bowls. These are pots encrusted in glass beads or rivulets of metal, some have collapsed and others are simply fascinating to look at, not that they’ll ever be used practically for food.  As always, if you have any material suggestions, I’m all ears and a huge thanks to Alan and Thomas, who sent me some of what’s seen in this weekend’s video. Thanks for watching! #experiment #pottery #asmr #oddlysatisfying #craft

lidded jar tutorial - part 1 (throwing the jar body and lid)✨ have to break this up into 3 parts because it will take weeks to go through the steps (we're making these jars in real time and rely on a community studio to fire) and I simply can't fit throwing, trimming, and glazing the jars into one reel 🥲 i find 200g is perfect for throwing the small jar body, plus another 150g for the lid. you'll see i throw my jar body and lid separately, leaving a lot of the refining for the trimming stage. especially with the lids, I find it easier to throw them roughly and finesse the fit once they're leather hard. i don't wire off the lids or jars, i wait until they pop off the bats. xo shan #pottery #potterytutorial #liddedjar #handmadeceramics #canadianartist

This episode of The Business of Pottery is actually brought to you by buttered noodles 🙃 These bowls aren’t the shape or size you picture of when you hear “pasta bowls,” they aren’t huge and you’re probably like “I def need more pasta than that”. When I brought the first one home I definitely didn’t think it was big enough HOWEVER, they fit the EXACT amount of buttered noodles to get me full! I’m talking about your mid-day bowl of buttered noodles or Mac and Cheese when you need something quick, not tooooo much, just enough to feel satisfied, but not enough to weigh you down. It’s the perfect size!  #pottery #ceramics #arttok #fulltimeartist

Maybe part of my own practice right now is learning to care less about Western institutional validation. I can take myself seriously as an artist without believing that a gallery, residency, MFA, collector, or critic makes my work inherently more important than someone making extraordinary pots as their everyday trade. Pottery is ancient, global, utilitarian, and deeply humble. I think a lot of us could stand to remember that.  #pottery #ceramics #wheelthrowing

Colanders, strainers, even berry bowls are quite popular. I make a few types of small medium and large colanders, but have really enjoyed making these strainer bowls. The shape is more of a basket or bassinet in which the strainer holes are only at the upper half of the bowl. This allows the fruit or veggies to be fully submerged in water before tipping and pouring out without spilling the produce. #pottery #studioceramics #wheelthrown #berrybowl #potteryartist
